description: Shared stable-text cases for the streaming protocol. Each case lists wire-shaped events in emission order and what the lifecycle guard does with each. The cases are replayed through the lifecycle guard, the session's reducer, and the reference reduce, not through a session. The guard is given no capabilities, so no case records a capability code (stream_exceeds_*, finality_level_not_reached); a guard that has an engine's capabilities, as in a session that an engine opened, can record more codes for the same events. Every event writes out finality, old_ids, new_ids, and extra, the keys whose default is not null, and every partial and final writes out stable_text. Every other key that an event leaves out is null, such as segment_id, text, and stable_text on a done event. The outcome of an event is 'admitted' (the guard forwards it), 'rejected' (the guard suppresses it), or 'invalid' (malformed: it fails event construction and never reaches the guard). The fixture runner skips an invalid event and goes on to the next one; in a session, an engine that fails to construct an event ends the session with engine_error. A partial or a final is invalid when its stable_text is null, is not the start of its text, or, on a final, is not the whole text. An admitted partial or final gives the stable_text as the guard forwards it, which can differ from the one sent; an admitted event of another type gives none, because it carries null. 'diagnostics' lists the codes recorded while handling that event, in order. 'display' is the reading-order list of [segment_id, text] pairs that the reference reduce keeps, partial text included; 'result_segments' are the texts of the finalized segments in the reduced result; 'result_text' is the text of the reduced result: the finalized segment texts concatenated in reading order with no separator. Each segment text carries the spaces and punctuation that join it to its neighbors, so no consumer adds, strips, or collapses whitespace. 'group' names the rule a case depends on: 'core', 'final' (a final is wholly stable), or 'supersede' (a supersede withdraws the retired segments, stable text included). The boundary cases cover only what the standard layer checks, that stable text does not end inside a combining character sequence or right after a zero width joiner; they do not cover the full rule that stable text ends between two user-perceived characters.

cases.name: growth
cases.description: Stable text grows from event to event; the final is stable as a whole.

cases.name: empty_stable_text
cases.description: A partial with an empty stable text promises nothing.

cases.name: shrink_is_clamped
cases.description: A partial whose stable text is shorter than before is delivered with the earlier stable text.

cases.name: non_prefix_is_invalid
cases.description: A stable text that is not a prefix of the text fails construction. The fixture runner goes on to the next event; in a session, an engine that fails to construct an event ends the session with engine_error.

cases.name: explicit_null_is_invalid
cases.description: A partial or final with an explicit null stable_text fails construction.

cases.name: rewrite_is_rejected
cases.description: An event whose text no longer starts with the stable text is suppressed.

cases.name: supplementary_plane
cases.description: Characters above U+FFFF are one character each; a cut between them is an ordinary boundary.

cases.name: emoji
cases.description: An emoji above U+FFFF followed by a space is an ordinary boundary.

cases.name: combining_accent_boundary
cases.description: A stable text that ends between a letter and its combining accent moves back to the nearest boundary.

cases.name: devanagari_vowel_sign_boundary
cases.description: U+093E is a spacing mark with canonical combining class 0. A cut before it is still inside the character, so the boundary moves back.

cases.name: zero_width_joiner_boundary
cases.description: A cut before or right after a zero width joiner splits the emoji it builds.

cases.name: boundary_clamp_stops_at_earlier_stable_text
cases.description: A boundary repair moves back only as far as the earlier stable text.

cases.name: combining_mark_appended_is_rejected
cases.description: A combining mark added to an already stable character changes that character: the event is a rewrite.

cases.name: closed_rewrite
cases.description: The closed restatement may reformat stable text once; its stable text is its whole text.

cases.name: locked_speaker
cases.description: Once a segment has stable text and an accepted speaker, a different speaker is suppressed.

cases.name: abandoned_at_done
cases.description: A segment that has stable text and is still open at done is reported; its text is absent from the result.

cases.name: not_abandoned_on_error
cases.description: A session that ends with an error is not checked for abandoned stable text.

cases.name: speaker_retraction_is_rejected
cases.description: Once a segment has stable text and an accepted speaker, an event with no speaker retracts it and is suppressed.

cases.name: speaker_first_assigned_after_stable_text
cases.description: A segment that had no speaker may get its first one after it has stable text.

cases.name: closed_may_change_a_locked_speaker
cases.description: The closed restatement is exempt from the speaker lock.

cases.name: closed_without_an_earlier_final
cases.description: A segment may go from open straight to closed; that closed final may reformat stable text.

cases.name: join_english_leading_space
cases.description: English segments: each later segment starts with the space that joins it to the one before, in its partial and in its final.

cases.name: join_keeps_announced_order_over_start_times
cases.description: Timed segments announced against time order: the reduced result keeps the order in which the engine announced them, the order an application displayed, and never sorts by start.

cases.name: join_first_segment_leading_space
cases.description: A leading space on the first segment, as the Whisper family sends, stays in the result text: no consumer strips it.

cases.name: join_chinese_without_spaces
cases.description: Chinese segments carry no spaces, and none appear in the result text.

cases.name: join_punctuation_segments
cases.description: A punctuation mark can be a segment of its own; it attaches to the text before it.

cases.name: join_whitespace_only_and_empty_segments
cases.description: A whitespace-only segment adds its characters and an empty segment adds nothing; both stay in the result.

cases.name: join_mixed_scripts_without_spaces
cases.description: Chinese and English with no spaces between them, as some sources write it.

cases.name: join_mixed_scripts_with_spaces
cases.description: Chinese and English with spaces between them, as other sources write it. Only the segment texts decide.

cases.name: final_stable_text_is_whole_text
cases.description: A final's stable text is its whole text: an empty or partial value fails construction.

cases.name: final_after_stable_partial
cases.description: A final that keeps the earlier stable text is delivered wholly stable.

cases.name: final_rewrite_then_abandoned
cases.description: A final that drops the earlier stable text is suppressed; the segment stays open and is reported at done.

cases.name: final_appends_combining_mark_is_rejected
cases.description: A non-closed final that adds a combining mark to the last stable character changes that character. It is suppressed as a rewrite, and the segment, still open, is reported at done.

cases.name: supersede_withdraws_stable_partial
cases.description: A supersede may retire a segment with stable text; the replacement starts with no stable text of its own.

cases.name: supersede_pure_deletion_of_stable_final
cases.description: A supersede with no replacement may retire a final, stable text included.

cases.name: supersede_closed_is_rejected
cases.description: A closed segment cannot be superseded.

cases.name: issue_81_case_1
cases.description: Two segments, each with stable text and a part that is not yet stable, are replaced by one segment. Its text keeps both stable parts here, but nothing requires that.

cases.name: issue_81_case_2
cases.description: Two finals are merged into one segment. No text is compared across the supersede, so the separator between the retired texts does not matter.

cases.name: issue_81_case_3
cases.description: Stable text replaced by unrelated text: the supersede withdraws it explicitly.

cases.name: reading_order_splice
cases.description: The replacement takes the retired segment's place in reading order, and the result text follows that order.

cases.name: abandoned_replacement_segment
cases.description: A replacement segment starts with no stable text. Once it has stable text, it is reported at done if it is still open, like any other segment.
